THE ROUTE, READ OUT OF vk/surface.c. update_surface_part()'s gate was `!current_binding || (upload && (pg_surface->buffer_dirty || mem_dirty))`. The `!current_binding` term is an UPLOAD term -- an absent binding must be re-resolved before a draw -- but it was not spelled as one, so it also opened the gate on DOWNLOAD calls, and the gate does far more than decide a cache hit: it unbinds, resolves the target address, evicts or creates a surface there, and BINDS it, after which the tail of the same function downloads what it just bound over guest VRAM. pgraph_vk_set_surface_dirty() sets pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty from `zeta` ALONE -- the per-binding flag below it is guarded by r->zeta_binding, the Surface-level one is not -- so the Surface can carry draw_dirty with no binding behind it, and pgraph_vk_surface_update()'s download branch re-enters update_surface_part(d, false, false) on the strength of that flag. There the gate was open BY DEFINITION because the binding is absent, and the call resolved a target from the CURRENT registers rather than from wherever the draw actually went. TestSwap() is the test that trades the two addresses, so the address the zeta registers name after a swap is the one colour has just rendered.
